title: Self-Supervised Combinatorial Optimization with Constraints via Frank-Wolfe
abstract: arXiv:2609.25728v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-supervised learning for combinatorial optimization has emerged as a promising paradigm for solving discrete optimization problems with neural networks, but a central challenge remains: handling hard combinatorial constraints within continuous, gradient-based training. Continuously extending combinatorial objectives to convex domains is a powerful technique, yet existing approaches often require projection steps that constrain neural network outputs to lie inside the feasible polytope and rely on ad-hoc and problem-specific constructions. We propose a general framework in which the neural network is allowed to predict arbitrary continuous vectors that could potentially lie outside of the feasible polytope. These predictions are then approximated by sparse convex combinations of feasible solutions using a geometric decomposition algorithm based on Frank--Wolfe methods and approximate Caratheodory results. translated_title: 基于Frank-Wolfe的带约束自监督组合优化
translated_abstract: 自监督学习用于组合优化已成为利用神经网络求解离散优化问题的一种有前景的范式，但一个核心挑战依然存在：如何在连续的、基于梯度的训练中处理困难的组合约束。将组合目标连续延拓到凸域是一种强大的技术，然而现有方法通常需要投影步骤来约束神经网络输出位于可行多面体内部，并依赖临时性的、针对特定问题的构造。我们提出了一个通用框架，允许神经网络预测任意连续向量，这些向量可能位于可行多面体之外。随后，利用基于Frank-Wolfe方法和近似Carathéodory定理的几何分解算法，将这些预测通过可行解的稀疏凸组合进行近似。这种分解诱导了……
tldr: 提出了一种基于Frank-Wolfe几何分解的通用自监督组合优化框架，允许神经网络输出任意连续向量而无需投影到可行多面体内，并通过可行解的稀疏凸组合来处理硬组合约束。
en_tdlr: A general self-supervised combinatorial optimization framework based on Frank-Wolfe geometric decomposition, which allows neural networks to predict arbitrary continuous vectors without projection onto the feasible polytope, handling hard combinatorial constraints via sparse convex combinations of feasible solutions.
